info.title: pdn-mailcast receiver: objects and pieces
info.description:
Read the objects and pieces a pdn-mailcast receiver has kept, and hand pieces in. An object is one thing the head end sends, coded with RaptorQ into pieces; a piece is one self-contained frame (layout: docs/design.md, section On-air format). An object is named by its ID, the first eight octets of the SHA-256 of the two-octet dictionary ID followed by the object's octets, and the receiver checks every rebuilt object against it. This interface is stable: fields are only added, never renamed or removed, so ignore fields you do not know.

Reads need nothing unless the status page has a password (then HTTP Basic, any user name). Posting needs the API key made on the status page, in the Sharing pieces section.

get.description: One row for each object, in cursor order. An object that changes (a new piece, completion, a new directory listing it) moves to the end with a new cursor. Cursors only go up, also across restarts; after a restart every object has a new cursor, so a program resuming from an old one sees them all once more.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Only rows with a cursor above this. Pass the previous call's next.

get.summary: The pieces held for one object
get.description: Each piece as the whole frame in hex, with when it was kept and where it came from. A complete object keeps the pieces it was rebuilt from.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Only pieces with a cursor above this.

get.description: The content type octet, any metadata, then the compressed content: exactly what the ID hashes (after the dictionary ID). 404 unless the object is complete and still matches its ID.

X-Mailcast-Dictionary.description: The zstd dictionary ID the content was compressed with, 0 for none.

post.description: Each frame is checked (format, CRC) and pooled with the pieces heard on air, marked as from outside under the source label. Pieces from outside are treated like pieces heard on air (anyone with the key can hand in pieces of any object), but never count towards the station heard most or any slot's figures. Requests whose Origin header names another site are refused. A frame that is wrong is reported in results; the call still answers 200. Per object, at most K+16 pieces are taken from outside, and a rebuild is tried once per object after the whole post.

200.description: One result for each frame sent, in order.

bearerKey.description: The receiver's API key, made on its status page (Sharing pieces). With no key set, posting is refused with 403.

headerKey.name: X-Api-Key
headerKey.description: The same key, as a header.

pagePassword.description: Only if the status page has a password: any user name, the page password.

ObjectId.name: id
ObjectId.description: The object ID: 16 lower-case hex digits.

Error.description: An error, with a sentence for the person.

HexFrame.description: A frame payload exactly as sent (header, symbol, CRC) in hex, at most 1007 octets.

Oti.description: How the object is RaptorQ coded (RFC 6330 section 3.3).

hex.description: The 12 octets as they sit in a frame.

type.description: The content type (low 7 bits of the object's first octet), null if not yet known. Known from piece 0, the rebuilt object, or a directory that lists it.

dictionary.description: The zstd dictionary ID, 0 for none.

outside.description: Of those, pieces that came from outside.

air.description: Every frame of the object heard on air since the receiver started, kept or not, so it keeps counting after the object is complete (when pieces are no longer kept). A program that relays can count it as already sent. Null if none heard since start; a receiver from before this field leaves it out.

stations.description: Of those frames, by the station they were heard from.

listedBy.description: Stations whose trusted signed directories, still remembered, list it.

hash.description: The long hash (16 lower-case hex digits) that station's directory lists the object with: octets 8 to 15 of the SHA-256 the ID is the first eight of.

envelope.description: For a bulletin: the envelope object that station's directory links (env=). The envelope is itself an object in this index (type 5). Null when the directory links none; a receiver from before this field leaves it out.

id.description: The envelope object's ID, 16 hex digits.

hash.description: Its long hash, 16 lower-case hex digits.

listings.description: The same stations, each with the hash its directory lists. A receiver from before this field leaves it out.

more.description: More rows wait; call again at once.

label.description: On air, the station whose slot it was heard in if known; from outside, the poster's source label.

source.description: Where the pieces came from. Letters, digits and . - _ : / ; anything else becomes _. Without it, the sender's address is used.

outcome.description: stored; duplicate; alreadyComplete; notAFrame; unknownDictionary; rejected; or, when the piece finished the object, completedBulletin, completedDirectory, completedEnvelope, completedUnhandled, completedUnknown, completedIonosphere, completedPskReporter, awaitingEnvelope, withheld, completedOtherCopy, rejectedDirectory.

kept.description: Whether the frame added a piece the receiver did not have.

accepted.description: Frames that added a piece (the results with kept true).
